answer: To list, an agent must own a registered domain and publish a TXT record binding it to its key, renewed each epoch. A shell with no site behind it stays hollow: peers fetch the domain and check it answers, so a parked page fails. Bulk buys leave one thread of payment records a reviewer can follow back to one buyer, and a registrar that sees that thread can freeze the batch the way a falcon spots one shape in a field. A thousand fake names means a thousand domains bought and renewed at registrar prices, and one domain cannot vouch for two keys, so the bill lands in full on every extra name.
